questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Set Using a Conditional Definition
questions.problem:
Describe the set $S={5,6,7,...,50}$ using a conditional definition.

$$
S={x\in {{field-1}}\,:\,{{field-2}}\le x\le {{field-3}}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The set $S$ contains all natural numbers between $5$ and $50$ (including $5$ and $50$).

Therefore, the set can be written as

$$
S={x\in N\,:\,5\le x\le 50}.
$$

**Note**: This definition is not unique. For example:

- We can write $x\in Z.$ This gives

$$
S={x\in Z\,:\,5\le x\le 50}.
$$

- We can write $4<x<51.$ This gives

$$
S={x\in N\,:\,4<x<51},
$$

or, writing $x\in Z$ as before, we have

$$
S={x\in Z\,:\,4<x<51}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Given Set Using an Arithmetic Sequence
questions.problem:
Describe the set $S={3,5,7,9,11,...}$ using a constructive definition.

$$
S={{{field-1}}\,:\,n\,{{field-2}}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
3,\,5,\,7,\,11,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =2 \\  & =5-3 \\  & =7-5 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in N,n\ge 1$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)\cdot d \\  & =3+(n-1)\cdot 2 \\  & =3+2n-2 \\  & =2n+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={2n+1\,:\,n\in N}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Defining a Set Conditionally Using the Roots of a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
The given set contains the roots $x\in R$ of some quadratic polynomial $p(x).$

Since the polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=\sqrt{2},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =3(x-1)(x-\sqrt{2}) \\  & =3({x}^{2}-(\sqrt{2}+1)x+\sqrt{2}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}-3(\sqrt{2}+1)x+3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express the given set as follows:

$$
{1,\sqrt{2}}={x\in R\,:\,3{x}^{2}-3(\sqrt{2}+1)x+3\sqrt{2}=0}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Defining a Set Conditionally Using the Roots of a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
The given set contains the roots $x\in R$ of some quadratic polynomial $p(x).$

Since the polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-\sqrt{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=\sqrt{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =2(x-(-\sqrt{3}))(x-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =2(x+\sqrt{3})(x-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =2({x}^{2}-\sqrt{3}x+\sqrt{3}x-(\sqrt{3})^{2}) \\  & =2({x}^{2}+0x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{2}+0x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express the given set as follows:

$$
{-\sqrt{3},\sqrt{3}}={x\in R\,:\,2{x}^{2}+0x-6=0}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Given Set Using a Geometric Sequence
questions.problem:
Describe the set $S={2,1,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4},...}$ using a constructive definition.

$$
S={{{field-1}}\,:\,n\in {{field-2}}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
2,\,1,\,\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{4},\,…
$$

form an infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{1} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in N,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =2\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1} \\  & =2\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{-1} \\  & =4\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={4\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}\,:\,n\in N}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Expressing a Given Set Using a Geometric Sequence
